annotationRationale: The question tests local adjacency restrictions and identification under rotations and reflections. Exhaustive case counting supports either standard representatives or a count using justified symmetry-class sizes.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct. No area repair is proposed.

review.questionCheck: With a red center, normalizing a required blue side neighbor and yellow corner leaves four inequivalent valid grids. Cyclic color relabeling gives four classes for each center color, totaling 12. Independently, the oriented count is 84, with 12 reflection-symmetric colorings, yielding 12/4+72/8=12. Choice C and the key agree; no contradiction is present.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Independently checked and retained both shared methods from 2025_AMC_10B_Q21: force-colors-and-normalize and count-oriented-grids-by-symmetry-size. They give useful representative-based and orientation-counting approaches. The LIVE Burnside calculation is covered by the second route's elementary class-size argument, so an additional Burnside method is unnecessary.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed adjacency-coloring and symmetry-counting nodes are precise. Combined addition and multiplication is appropriate support. Omitting the broader graph-models node is justified because degrees, paths, and general graph modeling are not needed.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct. No area repair is proposed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The forced chain follows the directed color requirements correctly. The bottom-middle cases give 0, 2, and 2 valid completions. Each completion has exactly one blue side neighbor of the red center, restricting possible equivalences to identity or horizontal reflection. Three reflections leave the normalized set; the fourth fixes its grid. Thus there are four classes per center color and 12 total.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly credits 2025_AMC_10B_Q21#force-colors-and-normalize and retains its inherited randommath-reference-2025_AMC_10B_Q21 ID. The current Random Math reference supports the route, and the candidate correctly applies the blue-to-yellow requirement throughout. Project reuse and third-party-informed provenance are explicit.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: Normalization is motivated, every table entry is explained, and the nonduplication argument handles the possible residual reflection. Cyclic color relabeling is correctly used as a bijection between distinct center-color collections.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: math:graph-coloring matches these local adjacency requirements without imposing proper coloring. math:symmetry-counting matches the justified representatives and reflection check. cnm_h232 matches the case totals and final multiplication.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The forced chain proves every blue side square has a yellow opposite, which establishes uniqueness of the blue side square. The exhaustive side cases have 3, 2, and 2 corner fillings, giving 4·7=28 per center color and 84 total. Only the axis through the unique required-color side square can fix a grid; exactly 12 oriented grids have that reflection. Rotations are all distinct, so the class sizes are four or eight, giving 3+9=12 classes.
